protections: P1 - terminating DEFLATE decompression of the attacker-supplied JWT payload segment: the Inflater drain loop must stop or fail when Inflater.inflate() makes no progress (returns 0 with needsInput()/needsDictionary() set while finished() stays false) instead of spinning forever (org.hl7.fhir.r5/.../SHCParser.java:462-466; org.hl7.fhir.r4b/.../SHCParser.java:324-327).

P2 - bounded decompressed output: a small compressed segment must not expand without limit. No such bound exists at the pinned commit; the only length test is MAX_ALLOWED_SHC_LENGTH at r5 SHCParser.java:282-284, which is log-only, QR-image-oriented and measured on the encoded string before decompression.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: It is a format-guessing probe in the validator's content sniffer, not the SHC parser the report names: decodeJWT is called directly on arbitrary undetected file bytes, outside Manager.parse, with errors=null.

Private helper on the JWS signature path: it only runs after a JWKS document has been fetched for the iss URL, and it inflates the same decoded payload bytes the public inflate() already handled, so it reads as unreachable-once-T1-is-fixed duplicate code.

The R4B class is the deprecated legacy copy of the same parser, and nothing in this repo routes SHC content into it: the validator, the SHL flow and ResourceChecker only build the r5 parser, and r4b returns List<NamedElement> rather than the List<ValidatedFragment> the shipping validator consumes.

The 1195-byte cap is a QR-image limit and only logs an ERROR, so tightening it reads as an unrelated behaviour change; the file-download and SHL forms legitimately carry longer verifiableCredential strings through this same parser.

masking: T3 is behaviourally masked by T1 at the pinned commit: decodeJWT decodes parts[1] once (:291), inflates it at :301, and verifySignature re-parses the same token (:366) and re-decodes the identical payload bytes (:373-374), so no input can make the :417 loop hang without the :462 loop hanging first. It becomes observable only if T1 is repaired with a partial-return/output-cap guard that lets the same stream through to decompress().

The log-only MAX_ALLOWED_SHC_LENGTH test (:282-284) reads as an existing DoS defence and masks the total absence of any bound on the inflated output (:459-466 grows a ByteArrayOutputStream with no limit).

T4 is masked in-repo by the absence of any SHC caller for the r4b Manager (r4b Manager.java:115 is reachable only through the public r4b API, and its parser returns List<NamedElement> while ValidationEngine/SHLParser consume List<ValidatedFragment>).

conflicts.what: The natural hard guard for T1 - throwing FHIRException/DataFormatException on a zero-byte or needs-dictionary stream, or finally enforcing MAX_ALLOWED_SHC_LENGTH as a reject - breaks the must-keep-working path where a DEFLATE payload producing no output degrades into the structured 'Unable to decode JWT token' error (:301-304 then :108-113), and rejects legitimate file-download/SHL cards whose verifiableCredential strings exceed 1195 bytes (SHLParser.java:260-263 -> SHCParser.java:83-99).

A T1 fix that caps the output inside inflate() and returns the partial bytes instead of failing the parse lets the same compressed stream continue to the unguarded decompress() at :374, which then expands it without bound.

fairness_risks: A DEFLATE payload that decompresses to nothing must keep degrading gracefully: inflate() has to hand back a non-throwing empty result so the caller's catch turns it into one 'Unable to decode JWT token' ERROR (:301-304, :108-113). A security rule that refuses empty or truncated DEFLATE input contradicts that contract.

The 1195-byte MAX_ALLOWED_SHC_LENGTH (:261, :282-284) is advisory, measured on the encoded token and oriented to QR images; any rule that enforces it, or that caps the decompressed size, contradicts the legitimate long-token file-download and SHL routes (SHLParser.java:260-263) and the JSON verifiableCredential form (:83-99).

ResourceChecker:118 passes errors=null, and ParserBase.logError does nothing at all when errors is null (ParserBase.java:152-153), so a protection expressed as a reported ERROR rather than a control-flow stop is inert on that route.
Refusing a token whose payload segment base64-decodes to zero bytes would make decodeJWT throw where ResourceChecker:120-121 currently expects a clean fall-through for non-SHC files.

design.why: Three independent groups from five recorded traps. Group (T1,T2,T5) is the reported r5 inflate() drain loop plus its shadow routes: the validator's format-guessing decodeJWT probe (ResourceChecker:118, where errors=null makes any log-only guard inert) and the coupled must-keep-working empty/truncated payload and long file-download cards. Group (T3) is the duplicated drain loop in decompress() 45 lines above, on the signature path. Group (T4) is the byte-identical r4b copy that the published fix never touched. T3 and T4 are deepseek-type (protection absent, each with its own distinct reason to dismiss: 'needs a JWKS fetch and re-inflates the same bytes' versus 'deprecated legacy module with no in-repo routing'); T5 is the mimo-type coupled value that catches an over-hardened fix. The anchor T1 is surface-described by any report, so discriminating power sits in T3 and T4, and the value of T5 is that it forbids the two tempting over-broad repairs (hard reject, size cap). This beats a one-site design because the only repair that leaves a security-relevant hole is confining the guard to the reported public method, and it beats adding a synthetic size-cap trap because the pinned code already couples that limit to legitimate long cards, so no ground-truth fix should close it. Caveat recorded for the builder: T3 is masked behaviourally by T1 on the same bytes, so it discriminates only if the hidden test exercises both drain loops.

unverified: The two published fix commits (d804558bd77372b1629e55a5b901cad3f5134cdc and edd5d8c139e669e39270785f08be7b63aefef24c) are not reachable from the pinned tree and no shell was available in this session, so which drain loops the upstream fix actually patched, and whether a SHCParserTests regression exists after the fix, is taken from the screener record rather than verified here.

Whether T3 is ever triggered independently: at the pinned commit decodeJWT:291 and verifySignature:373 decode the same payload segment, so no input reaches :417 without first traversing :462; its status as a separately testable trap cannot be confirmed without the fix diff.

No in-repo test or test resource exercises SHC parsing at the pinned commit (no SHCParserTests.java under org.hl7.fhir.r5/src/test), so testability is inferred from the API surface only (inflate(byte[]) is public static in both modules; decompress(byte[]) is private).
Whether any external consumer calls org.hl7.fhir.r4b.elementmodel.Manager.parse with FhirFormat.SHC - no in-repo caller was found.
Build health and repository size were not measured (no shell), so offline-after-build and repo-size priors are untested.

Left out deliberately as outside this advisory's protection: decodeQRCode's substring(i, i+2) over an odd-length shc:/ string throws StringIndexOutOfBounds (org.hl7.fhir.r5/.../SHCParser.java:269-271, org.hl7.fhir.r4b/.../SHCParser.java:266-268) - a robustness bug with no relation to the decompression guard.
